blocks.text: Sump pump installation in Castle Hills, TX, can be a great investment for your household. From protecting your home’s foundation to preventing unwanted mold growth, a sump pump can be the ideal solution to keep your home and family safe. We even provide sump pump repair services, so you can always get professional assistance when you need it the most.
A sump pump is simply a water transfer system that we typically install in your basement or crawl space.

When floodwaters enter your space, a sump pump will turn on and pump that unwanted water directly out of your home to a safe location away from its foundation. This pump can be a real lifesaver when it comes to maintaining the integrity of your home.

There’s no doubt that flood waters can have a huge impact on your home. Apart from damaging your foundation and encouraging dangerous mold growth, water can potentially damage anything it comes into contact with.

This means any electrical system components, like outlets, that are below the water level can cause extensive damage to your electrical system. Any furniture, electronic devices, or appliances that come into contact with flood water can experience permanent damage as well.

Investing in a sump pump is ideal for preventing many of these negative situations and protecting your financial interests. Our team of helpful plumbers can easily assess your home and recommend the best sump pump to meet your needs.

There are various sizes, styles, and power levels available to choose from. The size of your basement or crawl space, the local water table level, how much flooding you experience regularly, and the height of your vertical discharge pipe will all play a crucial role in determining the ideal pump size for your needs.
Your sump pump can experience issues over its lifespan that will require professional intervention. One of the most common is float switch issues.

The float switch on your device is responsible for turning it on and off depending on where the water level is in the sump pump pit. If the water level rises above the threshold and your float switch isn’t engaging to turn on your pump, it can create a real problem.
One typical reason your float switch may be malfunctioning is that there’s debris. If there’s debris under the switch, it won’t be able to move back and forth to engage the pump.

Sometimes, all you need to do to resolve the issue is remove that debris. If this doesn’t fix the problem, the float switch itself may need replacing by one of our knowledgeable plumbing professionals.
